answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a publicly verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before it can participate. Although GPUs can run separate chains in parallel, they cannot shortcut the dependency between squarings within one chain; creating many clones therefore demands proportionally more hardware or elapsed time. The echo of each prior result feeds the next, making a mirror identity costly to produce quickly, while an atlas of identities remains bounded by this physical bottleneck.
